interface.signature: def shortestDistance(N: int, M: int, X: int, Y: int, A: List[List[int]]) -> int:

preconditions.description: Matrix dimensions N and M are within the specified bounds.
Destination coordinates (X, Y) are within matrix bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= A[i][j] <= 1 for i in range(N) for j in range(M))
preconditions.description: All cells in matrix A contain only 0 or 1.

postconditions.description: Returned value is either -1 (impossible path) or a non-negative integer representing the minimum steps (bounded by N*M).

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 if not any(A[X][Y] == 1 and any(A[i][j] == 1 for i in range(N) for j in range(M))) else True
postconditions.description: If destination (X, Y) is unreachable (value = 0 or no path exists), return -1.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value == sum(1 for i in range(N) for j in range(M) if A[i][j] == 1) - 1 if all(A[i][j] == 1 for i in range(N) for j in range(M)) else True)
postconditions.description: If all cells are traversable, the maximum possible steps is (N*M - 1).

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value == 0 if X == 0 and Y == 0 else True)
postconditions.description: If start and destination are the same cell (0, 0), return 0 steps.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value == 1 if (X == 0 and abs(Y - 0) == 1) or (Y == 0 and abs(X - 0) == 1) and A[X][Y] == 1 else True)
postconditions.description: If destination is adjacent to start (horizontally or vertically) and traversable, return 1 step.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value == shortest_path_length if shortest_path_length is not None else True)
postconditions.description: Otherwise, return the minimum number of steps to reach (X, Y) via valid traversable cells (1s) using only up, down, left, or right moves. If no path exists, return -1.
